A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, On the Entropy Calibration of Language Models. Their main text, figures, equations, Appendices A–E, and checklist support reliable comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original singleton-mass simulations and measurements of language-model calibration, entropy trajectories, temperature and instruction-tuning effects, and generation quality.

after.justification: V2 retains these original simulations and empirical measurements in Sections 3–4 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: Future entropy scaling, its token-probability adjustment, backward fitting procedure, and Monte Carlo entropy estimation remain unchanged in Section 5 and Algorithms 1–3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate passage, story, and code completion using WikiText-103, WritingPrompts, and CodeContests. The synthetic power-law scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain Qwen2.5, Llama 3, Llama 2, and Pythia, with the same temperature-adjusted and instruction-tuned variants where available. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same model sizes, 5000 examples per setting, 128-token contexts, 1024-token generation limit, metrics, and temperature settings. Figure renumbering does not change the evaluation.

E4.justification: The singleton-mass simulations, temperature and instruction-tuning analyses, MAUVE-versus-entropy analysis, and example generations are unchanged. V1 Figure 1 becomes v2 Figure 4 in Appendix E; this is relocation, not an added analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains the same uncertainty display, and checklist item 7 retains the same explanation of error-bar reporting. Run-count, seed, and significance-testing information does not change.

E6.justification: All plotted data are retained unchanged, including the renumbered main figures and Appendix E figures. Reported scaling exponents, entropy trajectories, calibration-diversity findings, and Appendix D generation examples also match.

T1.justification: The definitions, Proposition 3.1, Assumption 5.1, Theorem 5.2, and the proofs and derivations in Appendices A–B are unchanged. Reflowing equations and algorithm boxes introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: Both versions claim slow improvement of text entropy calibration with scale and theoretical calibration without increased log loss under a future-entropy prediction assumption. The rewritten abstract and introduction preserve these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: V2 foregrounds error accumulation and the contrast with human-text log loss, but these explanations already appear in v1 Sections 2 and 4.2. Qualifications about dataset coverage, uncontrolled training mixtures, algorithm practicality, and possible Llama 3 tokenizer issues remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same software, quantization, smoothing, and GPU details; its only textual change is a figure reference. The code-access link and checklist disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged. Citations brought into the revised introduction already occur elsewhere in v1, and the relationships to prior calibration and error-accumulation research remain the same.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites parts of the abstract and opening introduction to explain the motivation more directly, makes small wording edits in Sections 2–3, and updates cross-references. The overall section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The singleton-mass and unigram-frequency figure moves from the main text to Appendix E, becoming Figure 4. Former Figures 2–4 become Figures 1–3, and surrounding text and algorithm placement reflow. The plots themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 explains the human-text log-loss contrast and error-accumulation mechanism earlier and more directly, modestly improving accessibility. The supporting singleton plot becomes less immediately accessible in Appendix E but remains intact. The benefit is editorial; the scientific evidence, theory, and limitations are unchanged.
